title: Add invocation ECDF latency rollups and journey tracing UI
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds ECDF-based latency rollups for invocation-level SLO analysis and a Journey Tracing UI panel to visualize grouped spans, log slices, and per-invocation token/cost breakdowns. Backfilled metrics for 7 days. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: existing percentile-only rollups obscure long-tail behavior and make it hard to correlate multi-span 'journeys' across retries and async steps. This PR introduces invocation ECDF rollups so SREs and engineers can inspect the full latency distribution, and a Journey Tracing UI that groups spans, shows contextual log slices, and surfaces token-level cost attribution per invocation. Summary of changes: 1) ingest pipeline: new ecdf_rollup stage that consumes sampled span/duration events and emits compact 64-bucket ECDF sketches per route+model+tenant on a fixed window; 2) store: expanded telemetry index with ecdf.sketch binary blobs and low-cardinality rollup keys; 3) api: new GET /telemetry/ecdf endpoint with fast aggregation and quantile extraction; 4) ui: JourneyTracePanel that groups spans into journeys using inv_id and heuristics (retry, fork, async), displays ECDF sparkline, and a collapsible token-cost table; 5) backfill: offline job to backfill the last 7 days of ECDF rollups. Migration notes: we add a compact sketch proto but keep old percentile rollups intact; feature is gated behind a server-side flag ecdf_rollups.enabled and Journey UI feature flag. Rollout plan: feature flag startup, enable ECDF ingestion for 5% of traffic for 48h, verify storage and query latency goals, increase to 50% then 100% with dashboard monitors. Testing: unit tests for sketch update/merge, e2e tests in observability-integration that validate ecdf endpoint returns expected CDF values for synthetic traces, manual QA of UI with synthetic journeys. Performance: ingestion adds ~6% CPU to the telemetry ingestion worker if enabled; sketch size tuned to 12KB per route-window to stay within storage budget. Related work: complements ENG-1680 (percentile heatmaps) and ENG-1899 (cost attribution). Context: this is aimed at giving teams better tools to detect fat-tail regressions and visually follow the sequence of spans that produced them. The description below summarizes notable implementation details and safety checks. Implementation details: the sketch implementation is a trimmed t-digest-inspired ECDF with deterministic merging and a known error bound for quantiles; rollups are keyed by {tenant, route, model_variant, window_start}; retention is same as other telemetry rollups (30 days hot, 180 days cold). The API supports percentile extraction and CDF series for sparkline rendering. Storage uses existing blob store with LZ4 compression. The Journey UI uses existing Trace service for span lookup and enriches spans with ecdf.percentile annotations when available. Observability changes: added dashboards: observability/telemetry/ecdf-overview and observability/telemetry/journey-explorer. Alerts: new SLO signal rule that fires when 99.5th percentile exceeds baseline and ECDF shows >10% mass above baseline. Compatibility: no changes to client SDKs. Security: no additional PII surfaced; token cost tables show aggregated counts only. Backward compatibility: old percentile panels continue to work. Ops runbook: steps to disable ingestion, how to backfill, how to rerun sketch compaction job.

review_comments: Liam: Can you justify the 12KB sketch size? It seems large for high-cardinality tenants. Author: We measured error vs size tradeoff and 12KB keeps median error <0.5% while staying within storage budget; we can tune per-tenant later.
Priya: The API needs pagination and time-range validation. Author: added validation and documented it in api/telemetry/ecdf_handler.go; tests cover invalid ranges.
Diego: UI looks good but prefer lazy-loading for token-cost table. Author: implemented on-demand fetch and added skeleton rows to avoid layout shift.
merge_commit_summary: squash: invocation ECDF rollups + Journey Tracing UI: add sketching, store, API, UI, backfill, gated rollout
testing_notes: Ran backfill locally on production-like dataset and validated ECDF sparklines match offline quantile computation
Load test: ingestion worker CPU +6% at 10k events/s, within capacity for default worker pool
Manual QA: exercised journey grouping across retries and async forks with synthetic workloads
notes_for_release_engineers: Enable ecdf_rollups.enabled=false by default in release; enable on canary hosts via infra toggle
Backfill job should be scheduled after enabling ingestion to avoid gaps; backfill script provided under scripts/backfill
